title: Request public records (Virginia FOIA)
question: How do I ask Staunton for copies of public records, how long will it take, and what can it cost?
office: City FOIA officers (one per records area; general requests to the City FOIA Officer)
summary: Virginia citizens and media that circulate or broadcast in Virginia can ask Staunton for copies of existing public records under FOIA. Send the request to the FOIA officer for the records area (police, fire, building, tax, court clerk), or to the City FOIA Officer at P.O. Box 58, by mail, email, fax, phone or in person. The City must answer within five working days, or 12 if it explains in writing. City charges are actual cost: $0.20 a page, $5 per USB drive or CD, and staff time after a free first hour; the Clerk's Office has its own rates. Estimates over $200 may need a deposit. If denied or ignored, ask the FOIA Council for an opinion or petition the Staunton General District or Circuit Court.

steps.step: Work out which existing records you want
steps.who: Requester (a citizen of Virginia, or a representative of a newspaper, magazine, radio or TV station that circulates or broadcasts in Virginia)
steps.how: Ask for records, not answers to questions. FOIA covers records that already exist, and the City does not have to create a new one. Describe the records with reasonable specificity: subject, date range, department, and any address, parcel or project. You do not need to say why you want them or mention FOIA. The City's FAQ lists the kinds of records it keeps (personnel, contracts, budgets, revenues and spending, real estate, law enforcement, community development, meeting records, fleet and solid waste, tax and licensing) and the exemptions it uses most often.
steps.quote: Your request must ask for existing records or documents.

steps.step: Find the FOIA officer for that kind of record
steps.how: Staunton's Public Records Request page names a FOIA officer for each records area. Building permits, inspections, building and zoning code violations, certificates of occupancy and site plans: Community Development Department. Fire investigation reports, fire code violations and hazardous substance storage: Staunton Fire & Rescue. Police records: Staunton Police Department, by email to SPDFOIA@ci.staunton.va.us. Business license and tax records: the Commissioner of Revenue's Office or the Treasurer's Office. Marriage, divorce, land, deed and estate records: the Clerk of the Circuit Court. Records the Clerk keeps as the court's custodian (case files, and recorded land, marriage and estate records) are requested from the Clerk under the court-records law (Va. Code § 17.1-208), not FOIA; the Clerk's other records are subject to FOIA, and the Clerk's Office publishes its own FOIA policy and rates. All other City records: the City FOIA Officer, P.O. Box 58, Staunton, VA 24402. The Commonwealth's Attorney and the City Sheriff take their own requests. Birth and death records come from the Virginia Department of Health, not the City.
steps.quote: The City has designated FOIA officers and staff to process requests for public records.

steps.step: Send the request by mail, email, fax, phone or in person
steps.who: Requester, to the FOIA officer for the records area
steps.how: FOIA does not require a written request, but the City suggests one so there is a record of exactly what you asked for. No City-wide request form was found. The Building Services Division (Community Development) has its own FOIA request form for building records, and the Virginia FOIA Council publishes an optional sample letter; the Council's best-practices guide, linked from the City page, has tips on wording. The City may ask for your name and legal address. Say whether you want to inspect the records, get copies, or both. You can ask for electronic records in any format the City uses in the regular course of business, for example by email or on a USB drive.
steps.quote: You may request records by U.S. mail, fax, e-mail, in person, or over the phone.

steps.step: Ask for a cost estimate before the City searches
steps.who: Requester; the City must offer the estimate
steps.how: Ask for an estimate in your request if cost matters. Before searching, the City must tell you in writing that it may charge its actual cost and ask whether you want an estimate. The response clock stops between the estimate and your reply. If you do not reply within 30 days of the estimate, the request is treated as withdrawn. The City's FAQ says an estimate also gives you the chance to narrow the request to lower the cost. Any cost of preparing the estimate counts toward the total, not on top of it.
steps.deadline: Reply within 30 days of the cost estimate, or the request is deemed withdrawn (Va. Code § 2.2-3704(F))
steps.quote: You have the right to request that any charges for the requested records be estimated in advance.

steps.step: The City responds within five working days
steps.who: City of Staunton: the FOIA officer for the records area
steps.how: Day one is the day after the City receives the request; weekends and holidays are not counted. By the deadline the City must either give you the records or answer in writing that: (1) they are withheld in full; (2) they are given in part and withheld in part; (3) they cannot be found or do not exist, with contact details for any other public body it knows has them; or (4) it is not practically possible to respond in time, and why.
steps.deadline: Within five working days of receiving the request; "Day One" is the day after the request is received, and weekends and holidays are not counted
steps.quote: The City must respond to your request within five working days of receiving it.

steps.step: If the City needs more time, it can take seven more working days
steps.how: To get more time, the City must tell you in writing, within the first five working days, what makes a response impossible. It then has seven more working days, 12 working days in all. For criminal investigative files the law allows 60 work days instead of seven. Before releasing a criminal investigative file, the police must also, with narrow exceptions, try to notify the victim (or, in some cases, family members or a parent or guardian), who then have 14 days to ask a court to stop the release; the response time is paused during that process. For a very large request, the City may also ask a court for more time, but it must first try to agree with you on how the records will be produced.
steps.deadline: Seven additional working days (12 working days in all), if the City gives written notice within the first five; 60 work days for criminal investigative files (Va. Code § 2.2-3704(B)(4)), with the time paused while victims are notified (Va. Code § 2.2-3706.1(F))
steps.quote: This will allow the City seven additional working days to respond to your request, giving the City a total of 12 working days to respond to your request.

steps.step: Pay any deposit or past-due FOIA bill the City asks for
steps.how: If the City expects the charges to be over $200, it may require a deposit of up to the estimate before it goes on. The deposit is credited to your final bill, and the response clock is paused until you answer. If you still owe the City for an earlier FOIA request that has been unpaid for more than 30 days, the City may require that payment before it answers the new request.
steps.fee: Deposit of up to the estimate when the estimate is over $200; any earlier FOIA bill unpaid more than 30 days
steps.quote: If the City estimates that it will cost more than $200 to respond to your request, the City may require you to pay a deposit, not to exceed the amount of the estimate, before proceeding with your request.

steps.step: Receive the records and pay the charges
steps.how: The City may charge only its actual cost of accessing, copying, supplying or searching for the records, with no overhead. Its published rates are $0.20 per page for paper copies, $5.00 for records on a USB thumb drive or CD, and staff time by the hour: $32.03 for the City's FOIA Officer, $39.75 for the City's Systems Engineer II, or the hourly rate of any other employee who does the work. The City does not charge for the first hour of staff time, and individual City departments may choose not to charge. These are the City's rates. The Circuit Court Clerk's Office publishes its own: $0.50 per page for printed and emailed copies, $5.00 for records on a CD or flash drive, and $17.50 an hour for staff time. No rates were found for the other constitutional officers (Commissioner of the Revenue, Treasurer, Sheriff, Commonwealth's Attorney). How to pay was not found; ask the FOIA officer.
steps.fee: City rates: $0.20 per page; $5.00 per USB drive or CD; staff time at the employee's hourly rate ($32.03 FOIA Officer, $39.75 Systems Engineer II), with the first hour free. Circuit Court Clerk's Office: $0.50 per page, $5.00 per CD or flash drive, $17.50 an hour
steps.quote: You may have to pay for the records that you request from the City.

steps.step: If records are withheld, check the written reasons
steps.how: A withholding answer must describe the volume and subject of what is withheld and cite the specific Code section for each category. The City cannot withhold a whole record when only part of it is exempt: it must redact that part and give you the rest. The exemptions the City says it uses most often cover personnel records, attorney-client and work-product records, vendor proprietary information, contract negotiations before award, tax records, health records, and appraisals for a proposed real estate deal. Police records have special rules: some records, such as criminal incident information about felonies, must be released, while criminal investigative files are generally released only at the custodian's discretion. Files in a case that is no longer ongoing must, on request, be disclosed to the victim, certain family members and certain attorneys (some only for inspection), whether or not they are Virginia citizens, unless a listed harm applies, such as interfering with an investigation or endangering someone.
steps.quote: cite, as to each category of withheld records, the specific Code section that authorizes the withholding of the records

steps.step: If you are denied or get no answer, ask the FOIA Council for an opinion or petition the court
steps.who: Requester; Virginia Freedom of Information Advisory Council; Staunton General District Court or Staunton Circuit Court
steps.how: No answer by the deadline counts as a denial. The City's pages describe no internal appeal, but you can raise the problem with the City FOIA Officer. The Virginia FOIA Council gives nonbinding advisory opinions; it cannot make the City release records, and it will not give an opinion on an issue while litigation about it is pending, so ask before you file. To enforce your rights, file a petition for mandamus or injunction, supported by an affidavit showing good cause, in the Staunton General District Court (form DC-495 is the district court form) or the Staunton Circuit Court. The City must have received a copy at least three working days before you file, and the court must hear the petition within seven days. If you substantially prevail, you can recover costs and attorney fees, unless special circumstances would make an award unjust. See the escalation section.
steps.deadline: Hearing within seven days of filing; the City must have received a copy of the petition at least three working days before filing (Va. Code § 2.2-3713(C))
steps.fee: $36 general district court fee for a civil proceeding (Va. Code § 16.1-69.48:2), if filed there; other costs, such as service of the petition, and circuit court fees were not verified; costs and attorney fees are recoverable if you substantially prevail
steps.quote: If you believe that your FOIA rights have been violated, you may file a petition in district or circuit court to compel compliance with FOIA.

escalation.trigger: The records are held by another public body, such as the City Sheriff, the Commonwealth's Attorney or the school division
escalation.next: That body's own FOIA officer, with a new request; if the City knows who holds the records, its response must give that body's contact information
escalation.quote: However, if the public body that received the request knows that another public body has the requested records, the response shall include contact information for the other public body.

escalation.trigger: You want court records that a court clerk keeps as custodian (case files, and recorded land, marriage and estate records)
escalation.next: The Clerk of the Staunton Circuit Court (or the general district court clerk, for its case files), under the court-records statutes rather than FOIA; the clerks' other records, such as administrative records, remain subject to FOIA
escalation.quote: Such records shall be requested in accordance with the provisions of §§ 16.1-69.54:1 and 17.1-208 , as appropriate.

escalation.trigger: The City says it cannot respond within five working days
escalation.next: City of Staunton, the same FOIA officer, which may take up to seven more working days; for an extraordinary request it may ask the court for more time
escalation.deadline: Seven additional working days (60 work days for criminal investigative files)
escalation.quote: If the response is made within five working days, the public body shall have an additional seven work days or, in the case of a request for criminal investigative files pursuant to § 2.2-3706.1 , 60 work days in which to provide one of the four preceding responses.

escalation.trigger: No answer by the deadline (a deemed denial), or a department's answer seems incomplete
escalation.next: The City FOIA Officer (P.O. Box 58), as an informal follow-up with the designated point of contact; the City's pages describe no formal internal appeal
escalation.quote: whose responsibility is to serve as a point of contact for members of the public in requesting public records and to coordinate the public body's compliance with the provisions of this chapter

escalation.trigger: Denied, partly denied or deemed denied, or a dispute over charges or process
escalation.next: Virginia Freedom of Information Advisory Council: a nonbinding written advisory opinion (send the question and the facts in writing by email, fax or mail), or informal advice by phone or email; the Council cannot compel production, and it does not issue an opinion while litigation on the issue is pending, so ask before going to court
escalation.deadline: None set by law; the Council says it will strive to answer a written opinion request within 14 business days
escalation.quote: Furnish, upon request, advisory opinions or guidelines, and other appropriate information regarding the Virginia Freedom of Information Act (§ 2.2-3700 et seq.) to any person or public body, in an expeditious manner

escalation.trigger: Poor assistance from the City in handling a request
escalation.next: Virginia FOIA Council's Requester Public Comment Form, sent to the Council, to the City, or to both
escalation.quote: Develop an online public comment form to be posted on the Council's official public government website, as defined in § 2.2-3701 , to enable any requester to comment on the quality of assistance provided to the requester by a public body

escalation.trigger: Denied, partly denied or deemed denied, or any other violation of FOIA
escalation.next: Staunton General District Court or Staunton Circuit Court: a petition for mandamus or injunction supported by an affidavit showing good cause (form DC-495 in the general district court); the City bears the burden of proving an exclusion
escalation.deadline: Heard within seven days of filing; the City must have received a copy of the petition at least three working days before filing
escalation.quote: denied the rights and privileges conferred by this chapter may proceed to enforce such rights and privileges by filing a petition for mandamus or injunction, supported by an affidavit showing good cause.

caveats: The City of Staunton's website (www.ci.staunton.va.us) refuses automated readers, so the city pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The Public Records Request page's copy of 2026-07-17 differs from that of 2026-05-11 only in a staff mailbox. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them or by phone before you act.

The City's Web Disclaimer & Privacy Policy sets no limit on quoting or reusing site content. It does say that email sent to City officials and staff on public business is a public record subject to FOIA, so whatever you put in a request may itself be released.

Fee schedule date. The FAQ PDF's link carries a version stamp of 2023-06-29, and the 2026-04-13 capture is that version. The hourly rates ($32.03 and $39.75) are tied to particular positions and may have changed since. No City Council resolution or ordinance adopting the rates was found, so they are recorded as the City's published policy. Ask for an estimate.

No local FOIA ordinance was found. Staunton's City Code is on General Code's eCode360, whose terms limit use to personal purposes and forbid reproducing content for public purposes . The table of contents of Title 2 (Administration) has no chapter on FOIA or public records. No eCode360 text is quoted. City Council agendas have not been searched. Under Va. Code § 2.2-3700(B), a local ordinance that conflicts with FOIA is void.

No City-wide FOIA request form was found. The 'FOIA Request Form' listed with the permit applications is the Building Services Division's 'Freedom of Information Request' (Community Development), dated 2026-05-05 by its link and its PDF metadata. It asks for name, address, email, phone, the location concerned and the information wanted, plus a signature. It has no fillable fields. The Public Records Request page does not link it, and the page that lists it has no Internet Archive copy. Use of any form is optional: FOIA sets no form.

The FAQs page https://www.ci.staunton.va.us/government/public-records-request/foia-frequently-asked-questions has no Internet Archive copy, so it is not confirmed. The Public Records Request page links the FAQs as a PDF (showpublisheddocument/226), which is the copy used. The 'Submit a Freedom of Information Request' link (i-want-to/submit-a-freedom-of-information-request) redirects, through ?navid=123, to the Public Records Request page (captures of 2026-07-17 and 2026-02-14).

Privacy: the Public Records Request page and the FAQ name each FOIA officer and list personal staff mailboxes and phone numbers next to their names (the general FOIA officer's number differs between the page and the FAQ). None of these are recorded. Only office addresses, role mailboxes (SPDFOIA@, circuitcourtclerk@), the Building Services Division line printed on its form, the City's main number, and court clerk office lines from vacourts.gov are given. The FOIA Council's FOIA-officer listing can confirm current officers.

Who may ask: Va. Code § 2.2-3704(A) gives the right to citizens of the Commonwealth and to media that circulate or broadcast in Virginia, and the City's FAQ lists 'Records requested by individuals who are not citizens of Virginia or representatives of the media' among the records it commonly withholds. People incarcerated in a correctional facility have no rights under FOIA (§ 2.2-3703(C)).

Response time for criminal investigative files: the City's FAQ gives 12 working days in all for an extension and does not mention the 60 work days that § 2.2-3704(B)(4) allows for criminal investigative files. The statute is given in step 6. Police records go to the Police Department's own FOIA officer; crash and incident reports may have a separate process.

Other custodians: the Commissioner of Revenue, the Treasurer, the Clerk of the Circuit Court, the Commonwealth's Attorney and the Sheriff are constitutional officers, and constitutional officers count as local public bodies with their own FOIA officers (Va. Code § 2.2-3704.2(D)). The City page lists the Commissioner, the Treasurer and the Clerk under its FOIA officers but sends Commonwealth's Attorney and Sheriff requests to those offices. Staunton City Schools (the School Board) is not on the City page and is not covered here. Court records the Clerk keeps as custodian follow Va. Code § 17.1-208 rather than FOIA (§ 2.2-3703(A)(6)). The Clerk's own FOIA policy page (Internet Archive copy of 2025-11-14) it gives the Clerk's own FOIA rates and names the Clerk with a personal mailbox, which is not recorded.
Payment: no page read says how FOIA charges are paid (cash, check, card or online). Va. Code § 2.2-3704(F) lets a locality offer electronic payment but does not require it.
Past-due bills: the City's FAQ says 'more than 30 days'; the statute (§ 2.2-3704(I)) says '30 days or more after billing'. The fee entry quotes the City's wording.

FOIA Council contact details conflict. The City page (2026-07-17 capture) gives 804.225.3056, an older number; the Council home page and its Advisory Opinions page (read 2026-10-11) and the October 2024 best-practices guide give 804-698-1810, and 1-866-448-4100 toll-free. The Council home page gives the General Assembly Building, 201 North 9th Street, 4th Floor, while the Council's own Advisory Opinions page and the 2021 Public Comment Form still give 900 East Main Street (Pocahontas Building), 10th Floor, and fax (804) 698-1899. The home page lists no fax. Use the email address, or confirm the mailing address and fax first.

Comment form link: Va. Code § 2.2-3704.1(B) calls for a link to the Council's online public comment form. The City page links a PDF copy of the 2021 form hosted on the City site instead. That PDF has no fillable fields (its form field list is empty; the check boxes and lines are printed), so it is marked not fillable. The Council's Forms and Sample Letters page offers the same form as a Word file (f6).

The court route is only partly covered here. The $36 fee is the general district court fee in Va. Code § 16.1-69.48:2 for an 'other civil proceeding'. Whether the clerk charges exactly that for a FOIA petition, plus service or other costs, is not confirmed, and circuit court filing fees and appeals from a district court decision are not covered here. Va. Code § 2.2-3713 states no time limit for filing the petition. The DC-495 is a general district court form; its instructions say it is 'Prepared by petitioner and acknowledged by a clerk, deputy clerk, magistrate or notary public.' Both the Staunton General District Court and the Circuit Court sit at 113 E. Beverley Street.

FOIA Council response time: no time limit is set by law. The Council's Advisory Opinions page says it will strive to answer written opinion requests within 14 business days, first come, first served, and that it will not issue an opinion while litigation on the issue is pending.

State law is current to Open US Law's copy of the Code of Virginia (for example, § 2.2-3704.2 shows 2025, c. 533, and § 2.2-3706 shows 2025, cc. 634, 671). Some quotes keep that copy's space before punctuation after a cross-reference (for example '§ 2.2-3706.1 , 60'). The law.lis.virginia.gov URLs are given for reference.
Local quotes keep the source's characters, including curly apostrophes in the FAQ ('City’s', 'employee’s'). The first-hour quote runs across a page break in the FAQ PDF; the page number is left out.
Fax: the City's FAQ says requests may be faxed, but none of the City pages read gives a fax number for a FOIA officer. Ask the office, or use mail, email or the phone.

Fees by custodian: the FAQ's rates are the City's. The Circuit Court Clerk's Office publishes different rates ($0.50 per page for printed and emailed copies, $5.00 per CD or flash drive, $17.50 an hour) and does not mention a free first hour. No FOIA rates were found for the Commissioner of the Revenue, the Treasurer, the Sheriff or the Commonwealth's Attorney, and it is not known whether the City's rates apply to them.

corrections: Quotes: all 84 original quotes confirmed. The 61 state-law quotes are whitespace-normalised substrings of I.text_of for the cited section, and every subsection label (A)-(I), (1)-(7) matches where the words sit in the text; rungs citing two sections match the first one cited. The 23 City quotes match character for character (curly apostrophes included) the Internet Archive copies fetched again by the verifier on 2026-10-11 with the research User-Agent: the Public Records Request page (2026-07-17; the 2026-07-17 183039 and 2026-05-11 captures differ only in a staff mailbox), the FOIA FAQs PDF (2026-04-13; link stamp 2023-06-29) and the Building Services form (2026-05-13). The live City site still answers HTTP 403, robots.txt included; it was not worked around. lexflow's checker (municipal.places.check_quotes) matched 64 of 64 code quotes after the edits, with 29 other-source quotes.

Nine quotes added and checked the same way: Va. Code § 2.2-3703(A)(6) (the clerks' other records are subject to FOIA), § 2.2-3706.1(D) (closed-case files must be disclosed to victims and others) and § 2.2-3706.1(F) (response time tolled during victim notice), against I.text_of; the Clerk's FOIA Policy (court records from the clerk, and three Clerk's Office rates), against the archive capture of 2025-11-14; and two sentences of the FOIA Council's Advisory Opinions page (14-business-day target; no opinion while litigation is pending), against the live page.

Completeness: the Circuit Court Clerk's Office, which the City page lists as a FOIA officer, publishes its own FOIA rates ($0.50 per page for printed and emailed copies, $5.00 per CD or flash drive, $17.50 an hour). The file gave only the City's rates; three fee entries were added, s8 and the summary now say the City rates are the City's, and a caveat says no rates were found for the other constitutional officers.

s2 and escalation rung 2: the rung sent 'court case files or other records kept by a court clerk' outside FOIA. Under § 2.2-3703(A)(6) only the records clerks keep as custodians of court records are outside FOIA; their other records are subject to it. The rung and s2 now say so, with a legal_basis entry.

s6: added the § 2.2-3706.1(F) victim-notice rule for criminal investigative files (14 days for the victim to seek an injunction, response time tolled), which the step's 60-work-day sentence left out; the deadline field now says the time is paused.

s9: 'criminal investigative files are released at the custodian's discretion' was incomplete. § 2.2-3706.1(D) requires disclosure of files in a case no longer ongoing to the victim, certain family members and certain attorneys (some only for inspection), subject to subsection E. The step now says so.
s8: 'some departments do not charge at all' overstated the FAQ, which says individual City departments 'may choose not to charge'. Reworded.

s10 and escalation rung 7: 'a sworn petition ... (form DC-495)' in either court. § 2.2-3713(A) calls for a petition 'supported by an affidavit showing good cause', and DC-495 is the general district court's form. Both now say that. s10 now adds 'unless special circumstances would make an award unjust' to the fee recovery and says other filing costs were not verified.

Escalation rung 5 (FOIA Council): added the Council's stated 14-business-day target for written opinions as the rung's deadline (not a legal limit), how to submit a question, and that the Council will not issue an opinion while litigation on the issue is pending (so s10 now says to ask before filing). Two legal_basis entries quote the Council's page. The caveat that said the Council's response time was not read was replaced.

Escalation rung 4: type 'internal appeal' contradicted the rung's own text (no internal appeal exists). Changed to 'delegation', the type fixtures/authority/ladders.json uses for the FOIA-officer rung (va.records.1).

Form f3 (Council comment form PDF on the City site): marked fillable false. Its form-field list is empty and the check boxes are printed glyphs; the caveat that said it has fillable fields was corrected. Added f6, the Council's Word copy of the same form, linked from the Council's Forms and Sample Letters page (HTTP 200 on a HEAD request).

FOIA Council caveat: the fax and the 900 East Main Street address are not simply out of date. The Council's own Advisory Opinions page (read 2026-10-11) still gives them, while its home page gives the General Assembly Building and no fax. The caveat now says the Council's pages conflict.
legal_basis § 2.2-3704(C) (agreement before a court petition): role 'deadline' changed to 'procedure'.

Contacts added from the Public Records Request page (office addresses only): Staunton Police Department and Staunton Fire & Rescue (P.O. Box 58), the Commonwealth's Attorney's Office (21 N. New Street) and the City Sheriff's Office (113 E. Beverley Street), plus the Clerk's FOIA policy page and the Council's Advisory Opinions page. The toll-free Council number now cites the Council's own page. Added caveats on fax numbers (none published for FOIA officers) and on fees by custodian.

Confirmed without change: the court clerks' office details on vacourts.gov (addresses, floors, phones, hours), the Council home page contacts, the DC-495 and its instructions (33 fillable fields; the 'Prepared by petitioner and acknowledged by...' quote), the sample letter link, robots.txt (the archived copy disallows only /scripts, /admin and .asmx paths for all agents), the privacy policy's FOIA e-mail statement, the redirect of the 'Submit a Freedom of Information Request' link, and the link version dates (FAQ 2023-06-29, Building Services form 2026-05-05, best-practices PDF 2024-11-13, comment form 2021-04-29).

Privacy: no staff names, personal mailboxes or direct lines remain (checked by search for every name on the pages read). The role mailboxes SPDFOIA@, circuitcourtclerk@ and foiacouncil@ are each published on the office's own page. 540.332.3862 is printed as the Building Services Division's line on its form and is the Community Development office line used in other Staunton files.
open_issues: All City content comes from Internet Archive captures (April to July 2026; the Clerk's FOIA page from 2025-11-14), because the live City site refuses the research client. Confirm the FOIA officers, rates and routing on the live pages.

The City's rates are from the FAQ version of 2023-06-29; no ordinance or resolution adopting them was found, and the position-based hourly rates may have changed. Whether the City's rates apply to the Commissioner of the Revenue, the Treasurer, the Sheriff and the Commonwealth's Attorney is not known.
No source says how FOIA charges are paid.
Court costs beyond the $36 general district court fee (service, circuit court filing) and appeals were not researched.
Staunton City Schools and the Sheriff's and Commonwealth's Attorney's own FOIA procedures were not researched.
The eCode360 finding (no FOIA chapter in Title 2) was not re-checked by the verifier; eCode360's terms forbid reproducing its content.
